user_input: I cleared the tier-1 tech interview today and everyone in the hostel wing was screaming and throwing a party in my room. I just stood there smiling, feeling like my own body was a hollow shell and I was watching some stranger win. I've spent three years grinding DSA, losing my sleep and my friends, and now that I actually got the high package, I feel absolutely nothing. It’s like my emotions got permanently switched off somewhere around third semester.

I sit in these group project meetings in the library, and everyone's laughing, making plans for the weekend, talking about their relationships. I literally have a 9.2 CGPA and I'm supposed to have my life together, but I just nod along like some pre-programmed AI bot. I don't feel angry or even sad anymore, just this cold, thick glass wall between me and the rest of humanity. I've forgotten how it feels to actually connect with someone without calculating what I should say next.

My dad called me today to brag to our relatives about my summer internship stipend, and I had to fake this enthusiastic, happy voice for an hour. The second I hung up, I stared at my hostel wall and felt this terrifying void, like I'm just an empty skin suit being paraded around for my achievements. I don't even know who I am when I'm not studying or coding anymore; I've completely lost the ability to feel real joy or grief.

I went to the college fest last night because my roommate practically dragged me out of our room, but the loud music and the crowds just made me feel even more isolated. I watched my classmates hugging, crying over old songs, and living in the moment, while I just stood there checking my phone every two minutes. I felt like a ghost haunting my own youth, unable to touch or feel anything genuine because my heart feels completely calcified.

I've been down with a high fever in my hostel room for three days now, and honestly, the physical sickness is nothing compared to the silence. People walk past my door laughing, talking about assignments, and not a single soul has knocked to check if I'm even alive. I tried scrolling Instagram to distract myself, but seeing everyone's weekend trip stories just made me feel this cold, dead numbness. I've completely shut off my phone now because caring about anyone or expecting them to care back just hurts too much.

Everyone in the wing is screaming and celebrating because they got shortlists for the Day 1 placements, and I'm just sitting here in my room staring at my open DSA coding tab. I don't even feel sad or angry anymore, just completely hollow, like my brain has shut off its emotional switch so I don't have to feel the shame of my 6.8 CGPA. I can hear them ordering pizza next door, but it feels like they are on a different planet and I'm just a ghost watching them through a glass wall.

I went to the hostel mess today and sat at a table with four guys from my lab section who were talking about their weekend trip plans. I was literally sitting right there, nodding along and smiling, but inside I felt absolutely nothing, like I was an actor playing the role of a normal college student. It's like I've built this massive concrete wall around myself where I can't feel their warmth, and even though I'm surrounded by people, I'm completely locked inside my own head.

My parents called me tonight to ask how my midterms went and if I'm preparing for the upcoming internship drive, and my voice was just so flat and robotic as I lied and told them everything was fine. I hung up the phone and realized I haven't actually felt a real, genuine emotion in weeks—no happiness, no sadness, just this dead, cold void where my feelings used to be. I am so tired of wearing this perfect, high-achieving mask when inside I feel like a hollow shell that might shatter if anyone looks too closely.

I was scrolling through Instagram on a rainy Friday night in my empty dorm room, watching stories of my old school friends hanging out at some cafe back home, and I realized I didn't even feel FOMO anymore. I just felt this cold, heavy indifference, like my ability to care or connect with people has completely withered away since I moved to this college. I am so terrified that this numbness is permanent and that I've lost the ability to ever feel close to another human being again.

We had a group project meeting today for our operating systems lab, and the others were laughing, arguing, and bonding over coding bugs while I just sat there like a piece of office furniture. I wanted so badly to contribute or crack a joke, but my throat felt completely frozen, and I couldn't find a single genuine emotion to project to them. I've become so disconnected from my own feelings that I feel like a foreign object trying to mimic human behavior in a room full of real people.

Everyone in my wing went out to celebrate after the placements announcement, and I just stayed back in my room pretending to debug some DSA lab code. I don't even feel sad or angry about being left out anymore; it's like my chest is just hollow, and I'm just watching my life happen on a screen. I talked to my mom on the phone for ten minutes and couldn't even bring myself to tell her I missed her.

I sat at the end of the long table in the mess today while the rest of the batch was loudly planning some weekend trip. I was right there, literally passing the salt, but it felt like there was a thick pane of glass between us and my voice wouldn't carry. I just smiled, finished my cold rotis, and came back to my room to stare at the ceiling because trying to connect feels exhausting and pointless.

My dad called today just to tell me that our neighbor's son got a 24 LPA package, and then asked why my CGPA is still hovering at 7.2. I didn't argue, I didn't cry—I just said 'okay' and hung up, and now I can't feel anything at all, not even for my friends who are texting me to hang out. I've shut down my phone because showing up as this empty, broken version of myself feels worse than just being totally alone.

I scrolled through the class WhatsApp group and saw everyone sharing memes about the upcoming midterms and laughing, but I felt absolutely nothing. It's like my emotions have been completely unplugged to keep me from losing my mind over my three backlogs. I want to care, I want to feel stressed or motivated like them, but I'm just completely detached from my own life.

During the DBMS lab today, the professor told us to form groups of four, and within two minutes, everyone had paired up while I just stood there like an idiot near the projector. Eventually, the TA just shoved me into a random group that didn't even look at me when I sat down. I used to care about these things, but today I just felt this cold, dead indifference wash over me, like I'm already a ghost in this college.

I survived the DSA lab test and actually scored a 9/10, but when everyone was high-fiving and planning a treat at the canteen, I just packed my bag and walked back to my hostel room. I felt completely hollow, like I was watching my own body move from a distance. I can talk to my roommates about assignments and placements, but it feels like there's an invisible glass wall between us; I'm physically there, but completely unplugged from their laughter.

My parents kept calling today to celebrate my mock placement offer, asking if I'm happy now that the 12-hour coding grinds paid off. Honestly? I felt absolutely nothing. I sat on my bunk bed looking at the congratulatory WhatsApp texts in the batch group, and it felt like they were talking about a completely different person. I've spent so long shutting down my feelings to survive this semester's backlogs that I think I've permanently broken my ability to actually feel joy or connect with anyone.

I went to the hostel terrace tonight because everyone was downstairs celebrating someone's birthday with cake-smearing and loud music. I could hear their screams and laughter, but it literally felt like I was looking at a movie screen rather than real life. I don't feel sad, just completely blank, like my emotions have been put on mute and I've forgotten how to unmute them to talk to my friends.

Everyone in the mess hall was talking about their winter break trips and sharing childhood stories, and I just sat there chewing my food, feeling like an alien who dropped onto this campus. I have a decent CGPA, I don't have backlogs, and on paper, my life is perfectly fine. But inside, I feel so disconnected from humanity that if I stopped speaking entirely, I don't think anyone would notice the difference between my silence and my presence.

I had a panic attack before my DBMS midterm, and my roommate was super nice, brought me water, and sat with me, but I couldn't feel any gratitude or comfort from her touch. I just felt cold, watching her hand on my shoulder like it was some scientific experiment. I feel like a monster for not being able to connect with people who are actually trying to be nice to me, and now I just want to lock my door and sleep for a week.

Everyone in the wing is screaming because they got day-1 offers at Amazon and Cisco, and I'm just sitting here staring at my LeetCode progress bar feeling... absolutely nothing. I cleared the coding round for a high-paying startup today but when my mom called crying tears of joy, my voice sounded like a pre-recorded voicemail. I feel like my body is here doing the DSA labs and attending PPTs, but the real 'me' checked out of this hostel months ago. I'm not even sad, I'm just completely hollowed out while everyone else is living in high definition.

I was sitting in the mess hall during dinner tonight while the rest of my project group was planning a weekend trip to Gokarna, laughing and passing around phone screens. I was physically sitting right next to them, chewing my cold chapati, but it felt like there was a thick sheet of bulletproof glass between us. I smiled when they looked my way and even chipped in for the bill split on GPAY, but inside I felt like a floating camera just recording their lives instead of actually being a human being in the room.

My roommates are asleep right now, and the only sound in this tiny hostel room is the hum of the ceiling fan and their breathing. I’ve lived with these guys for two semesters, we share maggi, we share lab manuals, but if I packed my bags and disappeared tomorrow, I feel like they’d only notice because my bed was empty. I’m staring at my phone waiting for a notification, any notification, but the screen stays black. I feel this massive, heavy block of concrete in my chest that prevents me from even reaching out to my school friends anymore—I’ve just drifted too far.

My CGPA dropped to 6.8 this semester and I have two backlogs in microprocessors, but honestly, I don't even feel the panic I should be feeling. I spent the whole evening scrolling through LinkedIn seeing people post about their summer research internships in Germany, and then jumped to Instagram to see everyone at the college fest afterparty. It feels like I'm watching a movie of 'college life' through a dirty window. I don't feel angry, or sad, or even motivated to study for my re-exams tomorrow—just completely detached from my own future.

My dad called me today to ask about the TCS pre-placement talks and kept talking about how our neighbor's son got a 12 LPA package. I just sat on my hostel balcony, watching the streetlights, saying 'yes, dad,' 'okay, dad' at regular intervals like a malfunctioning robot. He thinks I'm focused and studying hard in my room, but I haven't opened a textbook in weeks. I feel so disconnected from my family's dreams for me, and even worse, I feel completely disconnected from my own body—I look at my hands and they don't even feel like they belong to me.

My roommate is crying because she got a 7.5 CGPA instead of an 8, and everyone in the wing is huddling around her to comfort her. I failed my DSA midterm, my backlogs are piling up, and my parents are calling every hour asking why I haven't cracked an internship yet, but I honestly feel nothing. I'm just sitting on my bed staring at the wall, completely checked out, like I'm watching my own life happen on a broken TV screen.

I was sitting in the placement cell seminar today while everyone around me was aggressively networking and trading resume tips. I looked down at my hands and realized I don't care about the 12 LPA package, the coding rounds, or any of it, but I also don't care about anything else anymore either. I feel like an empty shell walking around campus, nodding when people talk to me, but completely locked inside my own head where nothing can reach me.

It was my birthday yesterday and my phone kept buzzing with 'HBD' texts on the hostel wing WhatsApp group, but I didn't reply to a single one. I ended up ordering food alone and eating it cold in my room while listening to the guys next door laugh and play FIFA. I wanted to go join them, but there's this heavy, thick wall of glass between me and the rest of the world that I just can't break through.

Everyone in my batch is planning this massive weekend road trip, dividing into cars and booking rooms, and I'm just sitting here pretending to debug my code so I don't have to look up. They asked if I wanted to come, but I said I had to study for a backlog exam because I knew if I went, I'd just sit in the backseat feeling completely invisible and draining their energy. It's easier to just stay in my dark room and feel empty than to go out and feel like a ghost in a crowd.

My dad called to tell me my cousin just got placed at Amazon with a huge package, and he spent twenty minutes asking if I'm even studying for my coding labs. I just kept saying 'yes, dad' and 'sure, dad' while staring at the cracks in my hostel ceiling, feeling absolutely nothing inside. I used to get angry or cry when they compared me, but now it's just this dead, cold silence in my chest, and I'm starting to worry that I've lost the ability to actually feel things.

I sat through the entire placement orientation today while everyone around me was aggressively networking and hyping each other up about tech stacks and 12 LPA packages. I literally felt nothing. No panic about my 6.8 CGPA, no excitement, just this complete, hollow blankness like I'm watching my own life through a dirty window. I nodded and smiled when people spoke to me, but my chest felt completely empty, like I've checked out of my own body.

I don't even have the energy to slide the curtain open and say anything anymore, it's like a heavy physical barrier has grown between me and the rest of the world.

I just said 'yes, everything is fine' in this flat, dead voice and hung up. I didn't even cry or get angry this time, which scares me because I usually at least feel some rage. Now it's just this cold, thick static in my head where my feelings used to be.

I know I was smiling and making the right jokes, but inside, I felt like a hologram that someone could walk right through. It's like I've forgotten how to actually connect my brain to my face, and I'm just running an imitation script of a normal college student.

Now, I'm just sitting here staring at my DSA assignments, not even caring enough to code, just feeling completely disconnected from my own body and future.

I don't feel sad, I don't feel angry—just this terrifying, quiet emptiness, like my emotional battery completely short-circuited and I've forgotten how to connect.

The hostel mess is incredibly loud during dinner, full of people shouting, planning trips, and laughing. I'm sitting at the corner of a long table, mechanically chewing my food, completely locked inside my own head. It feels like there's an invisible forcefield around me that stops any human warmth from reaching me, and I honestly don't know how to break it or if I even have the energy to try.

Everyone in the hostel is celebrating my 18 LPA placement offer, throwing water on me, screaming. But I just stood there like a mannequin, faking a smile. Inside, I felt absolutely nothing, just a cold, hollow space where happiness is supposed to be. It's like my soul checked out after the second round of DSA coding interviews and never came back.

I was sitting with my lab group today during lunch, and they were all laughing, planning a weekend trip, and sharing memes. I was literally sitting right there, nodding along, but it felt like there was a thick glass wall between us. I could hear their voices, but I couldn't feel any connection, and I just wanted to vanish back to my hostel room.

My feed is flooded with everyone posting photos from the cultural fest, laughing and tagging each other. I'm sitting in my dark room with a pile of backlog notes, feeling absolutely nothing—not even sadness, just a flat, dead emptiness. I don't know when I stopped feeling like a real human being who can actually relate to others.

During the late night terrace chats, my wingmates were opening up about their childhoods and exes. When my turn came, I just cracked some dumb joke to deflect and went back to my room early. I want so badly to let someone in, but every time I try to talk about how broken I feel inside, my throat just locks up and I go completely cold.

I took a sick leave today because my chronic anxiety just wouldn't let me get out of bed for the morning lectures. Watching the hostel corridor go completely silent after 9 AM made me realize that if I disappeared from this campus tomorrow, my wingmates would probably just think I went home and carry on with their lives. I feel completely disconnected from everything and everyone here, like a ghost haunting my own room.

I sat in the computer lab today for four hours debugging my DSA graph assignment, surrounded by 80 other people laughing and sharing placements updates. I felt absolutely nothing, like my body was just a shell typing code while my actual self was locked away in a dark room. When someone asked me for a pen, I couldn't even make eye contact, I just handed it over like an automated machine.

Everyone in the hostel wing is getting ready for the weekend trip, packing bags and playing loud music, and I'm just lying here staring at the ceiling fan. I can hear them arguing about who gets the front seat in the cab, but it feels like they are speaking a foreign language behind a thick glass wall. I don't even feel sad anymore, just completely detached from my own existence, like a ghost watching living people.

My dad called me today to ask why my CGPA dropped to 7.2 and if I'm preparing for the day-1 placement interviews. I literally had to pinch my arm to feel something while he was shouting, because my brain just completely shut down and went offline. I heard his voice like it was coming from a radio tuned to the wrong frequency, and I just kept saying 'yes, okay, yes' like an NPC.

I went to the college cultural fest today because my roommate forced me, but standing in that massive crowd of 500 students jumping and screaming, I felt totally empty. It's terrifying when you're physically there, but mentally you are miles away, unable to register the bass of the speakers or the smiles of your peers. I left early and walked back to my empty room, feeling like my soul has checked out of my body.

Everyone on my LinkedIn is posting about their summer internships at FAANG, and my WhatsApp is flooded with group photos of people celebrating backlogs cleared. I looked at my own hands today and they felt like they didn't belong to me, like I was playing a first-person simulation game of a failed engineering student. I've stopped replying to my school friends because trying to construct a normal human response feels like translating a dead language.

Everyone in the wing is celebrating. Sharma got placed at 24 LPA, and they’ve been ordering pizza and screaming in the corridor since 8 PM. I’m just sitting here on my bed, staring at my pending DSA assignment on dynamic programming, feeling absolutely nothing. I should be happy for him, or at least stressed about my own backlogs, but there's just this dead, cold silence inside my chest. It's like I'm watching my own life happen through a dusty window pane.

I was at the mess table today with five other guys from my lab group, and they were all laughing about some internal joke from the weekend trip I wasn't invited to. I was literally sitting right there, chewing on my cold rotis, nodding and mimicking their smiles so I wouldn't look like a freak. But inside, I felt entirely hollow, like if I stood up and walked away, my chair would just look empty and nobody would even pause their sentence. I’m physically surrounded by people 24/7 in this hostel, but I have never felt more utterly unreachable.

My dad called me today and went on a 20-minute rant about my dropping CGPA and how my cousin already secured a pre-placement offer. Usually, this would make me cry or panic, but today I just held the phone away from my ear, watched the seconds tick by on the screen, and felt absolutely nothing. No anger, no guilt, no drive to study for the midterms tomorrow. I’ve reached this terrifying level of burnout where I’ve completely unplugged the wires to my own heart just to survive the disappointment.

Some guys came over to my hostel room last night for a late-night chat, sharing deep stuff about their breakups and family issues, and they kept saying I'm such a 'good listener.' The truth is, I only listen because I have absolutely nothing to give back; I feel like a blank whiteboard. I nod and say the right things, but there’s this freezing barrier between my brain and my actual self that prevents me from sharing anything real. I’m terrified that if they look closely, they’ll realize they’re talking to an empty shell who can’t feel genuine warmth anymore.

I was scrolling Instagram during my lab break and saw photos of my high school friends back home going on a road trip together. Instead of feeling sad or left out, I just felt this bizarre, clinical detachment, like I was studying a different species of animal enjoying itself. I’ve been living in this campus bubble, grinding through coding questions and eating bland hostel food, for so long that I’ve forgotten how to feel joy. I'm scared that this engineering degree is slowly turning me into an algorithm that only knows how to execute tasks and nothing else.

I survived the DSA coding lab today and everyone was celebrating, but I just sat there staring at my laptop feeling absolutely nothing. I don't even feel sad anymore, just completely hollow, like my batteries ran out weeks ago and I'm just a ghost walking around campus.

Everyone on my LinkedIn is posting about their 12 LPA summer internships, and my dad keeps WhatsApping me screenshots of random cousins' packages with passive-aggressive emojis. I feel so detached from my own life that I didn't even cry when I failed the tech round yesterday, I just went back to my room and stared at the ceiling fan for four hours.

I go to the mess hall every night, grab my plate, and sit at the edge of the long tables hoping someone will say 'hey, sit with us.' Today my bench was full of guys talking about their CGPA and backlogs, but even when I tried to nod along, it felt like I was wearing an invisible cloak. I literally ate my dal-chawal in two minutes, dumped the plate, and ran back to my room because the noise of their friendship was making me feel so incredibly empty inside.

The hostel wing WhatsApp group has been pinging all night with memes and plans for a night-out, and my phone is literally vibrating next to my hand, but I can't bring myself to unlock it. I feel this weird, freezing block in my chest that tells me if I type anything, it will sound forced and stupid. I want to be close to these guys so bad, but there's this massive emotional wall in my head that makes me feel like I'm completely incompatible with human connection.

During the DBMS class today, the professor told us to form groups of four for the semester project, and my heart just dropped. Everyone immediately started whispering, high-fiving, and making groups, while I just stared down at my notebook drawing random lines. I ended up being the leftover person assigned to a random group of quiet backbenchers, and we didn't even exchange names. I feel so utterly disconnected from this college, like I'm just a ghost registering attendance while everyone else is building real lives.

I cleared the first round of the tech giant placement today. My roommates started screaming, hugging me, and ordering pizza, but I just sat there on my bed feeling absolutely nothing. It's like I was watching someone else's life through a window. I smiled and said thanks, but inside, I'm just a hollow, empty shell. Why can't I feel happy anymore? I've spent three years grinding for this, and now that it's happening, I feel completely dead inside.

I'm sitting in the back of the DSA lab right now, surrounded by 60 people shouting about red-black trees and internship shortlists, and I feel completely invisible. I can see my hands typing out code, but it's like my soul checked out weeks ago. If I packed my bag and walked out of this campus forever, I don't think a single person would notice or even care. I'm just a ghost occupying a seat.
